description:
The Companies Act 1993 section 4 solvency test, before and after a dividend or other distribution.

    Use for: 'solvency test nz', 'companies act solvency test calculator', 'can my company
    pay a dividend nz', 'solvency certificate dividend nz', 'section 4 solvency test
    contingent liabilities', 'section 52 distribution solvency'.

    Two limbs, both required: able to pay debts as they become due (modelled as cash plus
    12 months of expected receipts less debts due), and assets greater than liabilities
    including contingent liabilities. Equal is not greater, so zero balance sheet headroom
    fails. Cash $85,000, receipts $1,240,000, debts $1,180,000, assets $1,450,000,
    liabilities $780,000 and contingent $120,000 pass with $145,000 and $550,000 of
    headroom; a $200,000 dividend would leave liquidity $55,000 short, so at most $145,000.

    Args:
        cash: Cash and equivalents now.
        expected_receipts: Receipts expected over the next 12 months.
        debts_due: Debts falling due over the next 12 months.
        total_assets: Total assets at a reasonable valuation.
        total_liabilities: Total liabilities.
        contingent_liabilities: Contingent liabilities (guarantees, leases, claims).
        proposed_distribution: The distribution proposed; 0 to test as it stands.

    Returns:
        Headroom and pass or fail on each limb before and after, the largest distribution
        passing both, the binding limb, a verdict and the rules applied.
name: nz_company_solvency_test_calculator
